summary: In a warm Sunday-morning scene at Dr. Quelton's house, Lexy urges Captain Grey to stop accepting the doctor's restrictions and go upstairs to see his sister, who is shut away and not allowed visitors. Grey is reluctant to make a scene in his brother-in-law's house, but Lexy pushes him, and the two climb the stairs to the sickroom, where a nurse stops them at the door before Grey says he will look in on his sister. The passage builds tension around Lexy's suspicion that Quelton is hiding something and her sense that her own time in the house is limited.
one_line: Lexy pressures Captain Grey to defy Dr. Quelton's restrictions and visit his confined sister on a peaceful Sunday morning.
key_facts: The scene takes place on the veranda of Dr. Quelton's house on a warm Sunday morning, with church bells ringing in the far distance.
Dr. Quelton was courteous, affable and very attentive to his guests at breakfast.
Lexy believes her time in the house will not be long because she has caused Dr. Quelton an anxiety he cannot conceal.
Lexy tells Captain Grey that he is not allowed to see his sister, that no one can see her, and that he is not allowed to call in another doctor.
Captain Grey says that in her husband's house he cannot make a row.
Lexy asks Captain Grey why he cannot make a row, and the question leaves him startled and uneasy.
Captain Grey admits he does not have blind faith in Dr. Quelton.
Lexy advises Captain Grey to put on his best commanding officer's air and says there is nothing she would stop at.
Captain Grey asks what he can say to Quelton when the doctor hears about it, and Lexy suggests he laugh it off.
Captain Grey worries that Quelton might hoof them out of the house.
Lexy says Captain Grey is not a bit resourceful and says it is horrible to think of his sister shut up like that.
Captain Grey rises and says 'Right-o!' before they go upstairs together, the doctor having gone out.
A quiet, middle-aged little nurse comes out of the sickroom door in the other wing.
Captain Grey says he will just pop in to see how his sister is getting on.
